\begin{center}
{\Large\bfseries A two-piece construction for the\\[4pt]
$(2\alpha,\alpha,2\beta)$ family}\par
\medskip Denis Paliy\quad$\cdot$\quad 29 September 2026\par
\smallskip\small\textsc{Draft for discussion}
\end{center}

\textbf{Idea.} Glue a known triquadratic tiling to one quadratically subdivided
similar copy of the tile. The common side matches exactly, and the two angles
at one endpoint add to $\pi$. This gives every scale permitted by the elementary
boundary-length condition for the specified rational tile and target shape.

\textbf{Status.} Developed with assistance from ChatGPT and internally checked.
No external review or claim of priority is made. This result concerns one target-shape
family; it does not solve Erd\H{o}s problem 634 in full.

\subsection*{Theorem}
Let $0<u<v$ be coprime integers and set
\[
 a=uv,\qquad b=v^2-u^2,\qquad c=v^2,\qquad
 Q=b+c,\qquad P=b+2c.
\]
Let $T$ be the triangle with sides $(a,b,c)$ opposite $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$.
Thus $3\alpha+2\beta=\pi$ and $\gamma=2\alpha+\beta$.
There exists a triangle with angles $(2\alpha,\alpha,2\beta)$ tiled by $N$
congruent copies of $T$ if and only if
\[
 \boxed{N=k^2QP\quad\text{for some integer }k\ge1.}
\]
In the units of the specified tile, the target sides are
$k(c^2,cQ,bP)$. No condition $c<2b$ is needed.

\subsection*{Construction}
\textbf{1. The known piece.} Apply Beeson [1, Theorem 11] with
\[
 M=a,\qquad K=c,\qquad N_W=cQ.
\]
Its hypotheses hold because $a^2=c(c-b)$, hence
\[
 M^2+N_W=2K^2,\qquad N_W-M^2=2bc>0,\qquad K\mid N_W.
\]
The output tile is $(M,N_W/K-K,K)=(a,b,c)$. The theorem supplies a
$cQ$-tiling of a triangle $ABC$ with
\[
 AB=c^2,\qquad BC=aQ,\qquad CA=bc,
\]
whose angles at $A,B,C$ are $2\alpha,\beta,\theta=\alpha+\beta$, respectively.
Only this sufficient construction is used.

\textbf{2. The second piece and the join.} Take a $Q$-fold similar copy of $T$;
its sides are $aQ,bQ,cQ$, and its standard quadratic subdivision contains $Q^2$
copies of $T$. Glue its $aQ$ side to $BC$, with its interior in the opposite
half-plane. Match its $\beta$ endpoint to $B$ and its $\gamma$ endpoint to $C$;
call the remaining vertex $H$. At $B$ the angles add to $2\beta$, and at $C$
\[
 \theta+\gamma=(\alpha+\beta)+(2\alpha+\beta)=\pi.
\]
Thus $A,C,H$ are collinear, with $C$ between $A$ and $H$. The union is the
convex triangle $ABH$, with angles $2\alpha,2\beta,\alpha$. Its sides and count are
\[
 AB=c^2,\qquad BH=cQ,\qquad AH=bc+bQ=bP,
 \qquad N=cQ+Q^2=QP.
\]
The pieces have disjoint interiors by their placement on opposite sides of $BC$.
Individual subdivision vertices on $BC$ need not match: T-junctions are allowed.
For any integer $k\ge1$, scale the entire construction by $k$ and subdivide
each enlarged tile into $k^2$ original tiles. This yields $k^2QP$ tiles.

\newpage
\subsection*{Why these are all possible counts for this tile and shape}
The integer side triple $(c^2,cQ,bP)$ is primitive. Indeed
$\gcd(c,Q)=1$ and $\gcd(c,bP)=1$, because $\gcd(u,v)=1$; hence
\[
 \gcd(c^2,cQ,bP)=\gcd(c,bP)=1.
\]
Any triangle of this shape has side lengths $s(c^2,cQ,bP)$ for some real
$s>0$. If it is tiled by $T$, each external side is a chain of whole edges
of integer lengths $a,b,c$, so all three target lengths are integers.
Choose integers $x,y,z$ with $xc^2+ycQ+zbP=1$. Then
\[
 s=x(sc^2)+y(scQ)+z(sbP)\in\mathbb Z.
\]
Thus $s=k\ge1$ is an integer. Comparing areas with the construction above
gives $N=k^2QP$, proving necessity. No coloring equation is required.

\subsection*{The explicit 322-tile example}
For $(u,v)=(2,3)$, we have $(a,b,c)=(6,5,9)$, $Q=14$ and $P=23$.
The known piece has sides $(81,84,45)$ and $126$ tiles; the second piece
has sides $(84,70,126)$ and $196$ tiles. Gluing their length-$84$ sides
with the prescribed endpoint matching gives
\[
 \boxed{(81,115,126)\quad\text{tiled by}\quad126+196=322
 \text{ copies of }(6,5,9).}
\]
This is the $322$-tile instance listed as unresolved in the remark following
Theorem 14 of [1]. The known $126$-tile piece is also illustrated in [1, Figure 14].

\smallskip
\noindent\small The drawing is generated from the explicit tile coordinates.
In those coordinates $(x,y)$ represents $(x,y\sqrt{32})$; the four vertices
before a rigid motion are
$A=(25,0)$, $B=(-38,-9)$, $C=(-10,5)$ and
$H=(-580/9,115/9)$. The supplied exact-coordinate dissection has been checked
for congruence, containment, total area and pairwise disjoint interiors using
rational arithmetic. This computation is supplementary to the general proof.
